 FEZ / CASABLANCA (FesNews Media) — Fez-born Morocco international striker Youssef En-Nesyri needed just 180 seconds on Friday night, November 13, 2026, to turn frustration into vindication at Casablanca’s Stade Mohammed V, shaking off a disallowed 74th-minute strike to power home the Atlas Lions’ fourth goal in the 77th minute during a commanding 5–1 Group A victory over Niger in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers.
 Advertisement • Google AdSense 
 Introduced off the bench in the second half by head coach Mohamed Ouahbi amid intense competition for starting places from a surging wave of young Moroccan forwards, the proud son of Morocco’s spiritual capital and former Maghreb de Fès youth product delivered a textbook display of penalty-box resilience that resonated deeply with supporters in both Casablanca and his native Fez .
 Three Minutes of Mental Steel After the Offside Whistle
 Moments after entering the fray, En-Nesyri appeared to have marked his international return on the scoresheet in the 74th minute when he latched onto a delivery inside the box and slotted past the Nigerien goalkeeper, only for the match officials to rule out the effort for offside.
 Rather than allowing the chalked-off effort to disrupt his rhythm, Morocco’s all-time leading FIFA World Cup scorer immediately reset his positioning between Niger’s central defenders. Three minutes later, in the 77th minute , captain Achraf Hakimi surged down the right flank and whipped in an inch-perfect cross that En-Nesyri met decisively to make it 4–1, sealing the contest beyond any doubt.
 Advertisement • Google AdSense 
 Hakimi’s First-Half Brace and Bounou’s Pivotal Penalty Save
 En-Nesyri’s clinical cameo capped an eventful evening in which Morocco blended youthful exuberance with veteran composure. Rising striker Yassir Zabiri opened the scoring inside four minutes following clever playmaking by Brahim Diaz , before captain Achraf Hakimi doubled the advantage in the 27th minute with a thunderous long-range strike.
 Niger briefly threatened to derail the hosts’ momentum under Algerian coach Nabil Neghiz , pulling a goal back through a 41st-minute header and winning a penalty kick in the 44th minute. However, goalkeeper Yassine Bounou produced a decisive save from the spot to preserve Morocco’s lead, and Hakimi immediately punished the visitors in first-half stoppage time (45+3′) by curling home a direct free kick for his personal brace.
 Blending Fez Pedigree with Morocco’s New Generation
 In the 90th minute, 20-year-old debutant Ayoub Oufkir —cleared by FIFA earlier on matchday morning—rounded off the 5–1 triumph after connecting with an assist from fellow youngster Abdellah Ouazzane , lifting Morocco to a perfect nine points atop Group A .
 Advertisement • Google AdSense 
 With both Matchday 3 and Matchday 4 staged in Morocco due to CAF stadium certification requirements, the Atlas Lions now shift camp to Rabat’s Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium for Tuesday’s return fixture on November 17, 2026 , where En-Nesyri’s trademark aerial prowess and relentless mentality remain central to Ouahbi’s tactical arsenal.
